where: Lowtinder and Tinderwick Bay (the drowned old Tinderwick under the bay, swum to with Tidecall; half-sunk roofs, a cold bell-tower, one warm window: Gran Tallow's lamp-house) + the lamp-school's moss-garden
mood: The hometown lullaby, drowned: the same tune heard from under forty years of quiet sea. Cosy-melancholy, tender, a little haunted but never frightening; a music-box in an upstairs window.
_motif_note: Medium strength: this IS the Tinderwick theme (the classic is tinderwick-a's melody note-for-note, slowed and re-harmonised into A minor), so the remaster conditions on the shared motif; 90 BPM with a slow half-time feel (conditioning locks the 90 grid).
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
90 BPM with an unhurried half-time feel
a music-box carrying the melody, soft and glassy
a soft muffled triangle-wave lead, as if heard underwater
a deep warm string pad that swells like the tide
the gentle hush of distant surf
tender, melancholy, nostalgic underwater town theme

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {a single music-box note rings out alone, then the tide-like string swell rises under it and the harp begins}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the hometown melody, slow and clear, on the soft muffled lead over slow harp arpeggios in A minor}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the same melody again, now carried by the music-box an octave higher, like a song from an upstairs window, the strings a little fuller}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a warmer turn to F major, the strings swell like a slow wave, a little light comes in — someone is still keeping a lamp lit down here — then it ebbs back toward the minor}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the melody returns on the soft lead with the music-box answering each phrase; the last bar leads straight back into the main theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
